correctness.rationale: The n-th power splits orthogonally into n irreducible unilateral shifts, one for each residue r mod n, with weights a_(r,k)=prod_{j=0}^{n-1}w_(r+nk+j). Irreducibility follows from ker(V*)=span{e0} and cyclic orbit V^k e0; a single shift attains norm exactly when sup weights is reached. In a finite direct sum, intertwiners commuting with both shift and adjoint identify only unitarily equivalent irreducibles, so every reducing subspace is a direct sum of their copies and attains its norm if and only if all residue shifts do. Exact rational telescoping for w0=3/2,w_j=j/(j+1) gives norm-attaining S but all n>=2 products <1 with supremum 1; a second constructed sequence with initial weights 0.9 and later small odd weights yields S not in beta but S^2 in beta. Hyponormality is monotonicity of positive weights, and attaining supremum means an eventual constant tail. Exact finite arithmetic independently verified both examples; no finite shift truncation is used for the all-reducing-subspace theorem.
residual_risks: Strictly positive weights essential to irreducibility; zeros, bilateral shifts and arbitrary operators outside claim.

final_claim: For a bounded unilateral weighted shift with strictly positive weights, S^n attains its norm on every nonzero reducing subspace if and only if every residue modulo n has an actual maximum among the consecutive n-weight products. Power membership can be lost or gained. Within hyponormal positive-weight shifts, beta membership is equivalent to eventually constant weights and all powers belong to beta_0.
